fields.summary: Rewrite RDF generation framework for Java 8

comments.body: A. Soroka, Is this ticket still relevant given the recent Java8 refactoring?

Yes, certainly. No work has been done on the RDF generation framework. I would like someone other than me to do this, to ensure that we aren't getting a concentration of Java 8 expertise in one person.

As discussed in https://wiki.duraspace.org/display/FF/2015-08-13+-+Fedora+Tech+Meeting, refactoring RdfStream to use Java8's Stream API makes a lot of sense. Other such classes can be evaluated on a case-by-case basis.
RdfStream should probably be a subtype of Stream<Triple>.

My initial thought is to completely remove the RdfStream class, replacing it with a StreamUtils class consisting of static functions that return instances of Stream<Triple>. I also have defined a Collector for toModel.

I'm not wedded to that approach, but it seems like a good place to start.

The other component to this will be to create an Enumeration in kernel-api that defines a set of "contexts". Those values would be passed into the getTriples methods on FedoraResource, and it would be up to the modeshape implementation to map those Enum values to the appropriate implementing classes.
You should look carefully at what RdfStream is doing now. It is not an infinite graph, it is an infinite pointed graph. (See its method topic().) A simple Stream<Triple> isn't enough.
A. Soroka see a draft implementation here: https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/pull/962
